features: Line-drawn figure, front and back, with ten points to tap and the area lighting up in teal
Each point says what it usually is and what the physio would do, with the next three free slots right beside it
Four-step booking: problem, physio, slot, details, ending in a real confirmation card
Slot diary built from today's date, each physio's working days and a two-hour lead time
Real treatment-room photos, opening hours that read open now or opens at, and a book and call bar on phones
name: Fern Physio
short: A drawn body with ten tappable points, and a booking flow behind it.
long: A two-room physiotherapy clinic where the hero is a line-drawn standing figure, front and back, with ten points you can tap. Each one names what the problem usually turns out to be and what the physio would actually do, and the next three free slots for that area sit right beside it, one tap from booked. Real treatment photos, the price list and both physios follow on a crisp white page. The diary is generated from the real clock, so the slots are never stale.
proves: A visitor can say where it hurts before they have to say anything to a receptionist.
story: Clinics lose people at the phone call, because a sore shoulder is hard to describe to a stranger. Pointing at a drawing is not.
